name: Skyline Divide Route
approach: From Glacier, WA, drive Mt. Baker Highway (SR 542) east about 1 mile past the Glacier Public Service Center to Glacier Creek Road (FS 39); turn right, then take an immediate left onto Deadhorse Road (FS 37). FS 37 normally continues 12.7 miles to the Skyline Divide Trailhead. FS 37 has been closed to vehicles at mile 0.03 since 1 June 2026 while the 2021 flood washout at milepost 3.1 is repaired, with no end date given on the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest alert still posted on 25 September 2026, so the trailhead is not reachable by vehicle. When open, hike Skyline Divide Trail #678 through old-growth forest switchbacks and into meadows on the ridge crest (~2 mi), follow the crest to the trail's high point (~6,563 ft, ~4.5 mi), then continue cross-country along the open ridge to Chowder Ridge and the base of Hadley Peak.

approach_variants.name: Skyline Divide Trail #678 and the long open ridge south to Chowder Ridge
approach_variants.notes:
Access first: from Glacier, WA drive SR-542 about a mile past the Glacier Public Service Center to Glacier Creek Road (FS-39), turn right, then immediately left onto Deadhorse Road (FS-37). FS-37 normally runs 12.7 miles to the Skyline Divide trailhead. FS-37 has been closed to vehicles at mile 0.03 since June 1, 2026 while the 2021 flood washout at milepost 3.1 is repaired, with no end date given on the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest alert still posted on September 26, 2026, so the trailhead is not reachable by vehicle. Confirm before planning around it.

When open, Skyline Divide Trail #678 climbs through old-growth switchbacks into meadows and reaches the ridge crest at about 2 miles and its high point near 6,563 ft at about 4.5 miles. From there the route is cross-country along the open ridge — roughly three miles of it — to Chowder Ridge and the base of Hadley's summit block.

The trail's high point on the crest near 6,563 ft is the landmark parties use to re-find the maintained trail on the way back.
approach_variants.season: Roughly Aug-Oct — this trailhead may not currently be reachable at all
hazards: FS-37 closed at mile 0.03 during washout repair — the trailhead is not drivable until the work ends
Three miles of cross-country open ridge with no tread and no cairns
A short Class 3 step above loose scree and talus
Two unmarked divides converging on one summit, with very different roads at the bottom
No water once past the meadows
approach_variants.baseFinding:
The 6,600 ft viewpoint is the gate, in both directions. It is where maintained trail ends and where you rejoin it. In cloud it is the only reliable waypoint on this approach, because everything beyond it is three miles of undifferentiated open ridge. Note it on the way out — parties who do not, spend the return walking a crest that all looks the same.

The crest is the handrail. From the viewpoint the route runs south along the ridge and then southeast along Chowder Ridge, roughly three miles in all. Keep the crest under your feet with air on both sides; this ridge has heather benches falling away either side and it is easy to drift onto one and lose the line.

Arrival at the climbing: the summit block is a short class 3 step above loose scree and talus — the last stretch of the day and the only scrambling on it. Walking stops, one short step of rock, summit. That is the whole climb, and it is the test: if you are scrambling for a long time, you are on a false feature; if you have not left your feet, you are not there.

The discriminator against the other approach to this same block: Cougar Divide arrives on Chowder Ridge from the north-west after crossing near Dobbs Creek, and its trail high point is 5,920 ft. Skyline arrives from the west after roughly three miles of ridge from a 6,600 ft viewpoint. If you are descending in poor visibility, going down the wrong divide puts you 11 miles of gravel road away from your car on a road that may itself be washed out.

access.fees: $5/vehicle day-use fee at the trailhead, or annual Recreation/Interagency Pass
access.rules: Pack out human waste (blue bags) — no burial or glacier deposition. The route stays inside Mount Baker Wilderness, where party size is capped at 12 and campfires are prohibited.
access.closures: Skyline Divide Trailhead is not reachable by vehicle: FS Road 37 (Deadhorse Road) has been closed at mile 0.03 since 1 June 2026 for flood-damage repair, with heavy equipment on the road and no end date given, as listed on the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest alert still posted on 25 September 2026.
access.landManager: USDA Forest Service, Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mount Baker Wilderness)
access.land_manager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District) — Mount Baker Wilderness
access.parking_pass: Northwest Forest Pass required at most trailheads — $30/year or $5/day.
access.passRequired: Northwest Forest Pass or other accepted Interagency Pass

overnight_permit.where: No climbing or wilderness permit. A recreation pass is needed to park at the Skyline Divide trailhead; buy it ahead or on the Recreation.gov app.

road.name: Deadhorse Road (Forest Service Road 37)
road.status: Closed to vehicles at mile 0.03 since 1 June 2026 while flood-damage repair is under way, with no end date given, as listed on the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest alert still posted on 25 September 2026
road.driveNote: From Glacier, drive SR 542 east about 1 mile, turn right onto Glacier Creek Road (FS 39), then take an immediate left onto Deadhorse Road (FS 37); FS 37 normally continues 12.7 miles to the Skyline Divide Trailhead, but has been gated at mile 0.03 for flood-damage repair since 1 June 2026, with no end date given.
road.seasonalGate: No routine seasonal gate reported for FS 37 itself; access is presently blocked by the repair closure regardless of season
